question: Which of the following countries withdrew from the International Criminal Court (ICC) in April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hungary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hungary withdrew from the International Criminal Court (ICC) in April 2025, citing disagreements with the court's jurisdiction over certain cases.
 
• The ICC, established in 2002 under the Rome Statute, is a permanent international tribunal to prosecute individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes.
 
• Hungary's withdrawal was a move aligned with its stance on sovereignty and legal independence in international law.
 
• This decision drew criticism from various human rights organizations, emphasizing the importance of global cooperation in addressing international crimes.
 
• Hungary’s government argued that the ICC's operations were inconsistent with its national interests and policies in recent years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Criminal Court (ICC):**

 
 
• Established by the Rome Statute in 1998 and began operations in 2002.
 
• Headquartered in The Hague, Netherlands, it prosecutes individuals, not states.
 
• Its jurisdiction includes crimes of genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and crimes of aggression.
 
• As of 2023, 123 countries are parties to the Rome Statute.
 
 
 
• **Rome Statute:**
 
 
• The founding treaty of the ICC, adopted in 1998, defines the court's jurisdiction, structure, and functioning.
 
• Countries that ratify the statute become members of the ICC, agreeing to cooperate and abide by its rulings.
 
 
 
• **State Sovereignty vs. International Law:**
 
 
• Debates often arise when international institutions like the ICC intervene in national legal matters.
 
• Some states view such interventions as encroachments on their sovereignty.
 
 
 
• **Withdrawal Process:**
 
 
• A country can withdraw from the Rome Statute by notifying the United Nations Secretary-General.
 
• Withdrawal becomes effective one year after the notification.
